about.founderStory:
For nine years I worked alongside US accounting firms from India, and I kept seeing the same thing go wrong. A firm would hire an offshore bookkeeper, get a different person every few months, and quietly give up on the idea.

The work was rarely the problem. The problem was that nobody owned it. Staff were shared across five firms at once, so they never learned how any single firm liked things done.

Then a two-partner firm in Ohio told me they had turned away eleven clients in one year because they could not hire fast enough. That stayed with me. They did not need another vendor. They needed one person who arrived each morning already knowing their clients.

So we built tryACOwork around exactly that. One bookkeeper, one firm, for years. We publish our prices, you meet the person before you commit, and the review always stays yours.

professionalStandardsSignOff.note: The client decided on 23 August to publish without a sign-off on file, so the [CONFIRM WITH US CPA] markers no longer render. CO-10 recommended one. The copy is hedged - it opens by saying it is a summary, not legal advice, and to confirm your own position with your adviser or state board - and that hedge is what makes publishing it defensible. Getting a CPA to read it remains worth doing; it is now a recommendation rather than a launch blocker.
